claims.text: A post-deposition nitrogen anneal forms a CrN interphase at the Cr/Zr interface.
The resulting CrN interphase is nanometric.
Annealing in nitrogen at approximately 500°C for several hours can produce the proposed interfacial CrN layer.
The CrN interphase acts as a diffusion barrier to Cr–Zr interdiffusion during elevated-temperature exposure.
CrN has high thermal stability under the relevant exposure conditions.
The CrN interphase lowers atomic mobility at the Cr/Zr interface.
Lower interfacial atomic mobility retards diffusion of Cr into the zirconium alloy.
The nitrogen-annealed coating will show markedly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will enhance coating integrity during routine operation and transient accident exposure.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will enhance coating adhesion during routine operation and transient accident exposure.
The CrN-modified coating will preserve protective performance in subcritical water at approximately 350°C.
The CrN-modified coating will preserve protective performance in transient high-temperature steam up to approximately 1150°C.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating on zirconium alloy is prone to premature failure caused by elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed accident-condition performance boundary includes high-temperature steam transients lasting up to approximately one hour.
